query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Directly the target quantity (time to resolve), derivable from opened_at and closed_at. This is the core outcome variable for the query. NULLs correspond to open/unclosed incidents, which is correct behaviour.

per_column.name: priority_score
per_column.rationale: Numeric encoding of the existing priority column; useful as a modeling/grouping signal for resolution time, though largely redundant with the original priority field. Values are grounded in that column.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Category-level mean resolution time gives a genuine grouping signal (some categories resolve slower). Derived aggregate from in-table data, though it leaks the target and is per-category constant.

per_column.name: assignee_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Assignee historical average resolution time is a plausible predictive signal for slow resolution and is derivable by aggregating over assigned_to. Reasonable target-encoding style feature.

per_column.name: group_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Assignment-group average resolution time; a legitimate new axis to compare which teams are slower. Grounded aggregate over assignment_group.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Extracted hour from opened_at; a plausible temporal signal for resolution delay. Values are a sound reading of the timestamp.

per_column.name: is_afterhours_open
per_column.rationale: After-hours flag is a reasonable, non-constant signal potentially correlated with slower resolution; derivable from opened_at hour.

per_column.name: is_weekend_open
per_column.rationale: Weekend-open flag is a sensible signal for delayed resolution and is directly derivable from the opened date.

per_column.name: description_length
per_column.rationale: Raw character length of short_description is a generic surface feature with weak analytical leverage for this query, though trivially grounded in the text.

per_column.name: is_unassigned
per_column.rationale: Unassigned flag is a meaningful, non-constant signal—unassigned tickets plausibly linger longer. Derivable from assigned_to being empty.

judge.rationale: Most added columns give genuine axes (resolution time, priority, category/assignee/group historical averages, temporal and assignment flags) directly relevant to why an incident resolves slowly, and their values are soundly derivable from in-table timestamps and categorical fields. Weaker points: priority_score is largely redundant with the original priority column, and description_length is a generic surface feature with little leverage for this query. No hallucinations observed in the samples; NULL resolution_hours for open incidents is correct behaviour.
